title: Agent Scene
description: Machine-readable schema for *.scene.json in Agent Scenes 1.0.0. A scene is a pure-data bundle that configures a session for one stage of work: execution posture, skills, task brief, expected artifacts, exit criteria, and declarative hooks. The Agent Scenes specification (docs/reference/scenes.md) defines the semantic and operational requirements.

localizations.description: Display strings per BCP 47 tag. The host picks the best match for the UI locale; `title`/`description` at the top level are the fallback.

execution.description: Execution posture. Every field is optional; an unset field inherits the session's current value (or the project/user default at session creation). See docs/reference/scenes.md §Binding for which fields apply mid-session vs. only at session creation.

providers.description: Provider ids in preference order (e.g. ["claude_code", "codex"]). The host uses the first installed entry; an empty or absent list inherits.

pinned.description: Skill references (see docs/reference/scenes.md §Skill references) surfaced first in the `/` picker while the scene is active. Mcp skills among them are attached at session creation.

inline.description: Fragments defined in-scene, unconditionally prepended to every prompt compiled under this scene (after project rules, before the brief).

suppress_unpinned.description: When true, the `/` picker shows only pinned and inline skills by default (a "show all" affordance must remain reachable). Default false.

brief.description: The task-brief skeleton offered in the composer when the scene activates on an empty document.

template.description: Markdown skeleton. `{{slot-id}}` placeholders are rendered as fillable fields per `slots`.

clarify.description: How the agent should resolve an underspecified brief: structured multiple-choice questions (default), free-form questions, or proceed without asking.

artifacts.description: Outputs this scene is expected to produce. Required artifacts feed the default exit criterion and the pipeline carry mechanism.

template.description: Markdown skeleton the agent is instructed to follow when producing this artifact.

criteria.description: All listed criteria must hold before the host surfaces the scene-complete suggestion. Absent criteria default to [{"kind": "required_artifacts"}, {"kind": "user_confirm"}].

next.description: Scenes to suggest when the exit criteria hold. `carry` names this scene's artifacts to compile into the next scene's context.

hooks.description: Declarative event bindings. Actions are limited to the allowlist below; a scene can never execute arbitrary commands. `schedule` hooks are inert until the user enables scheduling for the project.

schedule.description: Five-field cron expression. Only meaningful (and required) when `on` is "schedule".

args.description: Slot values for `run_macro`, keyed by slot name. Values may reference artifacts as {{artifact:<id>}}.

guardrails.description: Short imperative rules injected with the scene's inline fragments (e.g. "Do not modify files; produce findings instead."). Guardrails are prompt-level guidance; `execution.session_mode` remains the enforcement boundary.

tools.description: Advisory tool-name hints forwarded to providers that support tool gating. Not an enforcement boundary.

extensions.description: Vendor extensions, namespaced by reverse-DNS or product key. Hosts must ignore unknown extensions.

skillRef.description: A skill reference: a bare library id, `harness:<harness>:<skill-dir>`, or `<plugin-id>:<component>:<slug>`. Resolution and precedence are defined in docs/reference/scenes.md §Skill references.

sceneRef.description: A scene reference: a bare scene name resolved by precedence (project > user > plugin > builtin), or `<source>:<name>` to pin the source.
